options.content: JVM whitebox for the Kotlin reports service (RFC-0001 D2 JVM showcase). Phase 6 PR-1 ships the skeleton panels below from metrics the service already exposes at `/metrics`. The **GC sawtooth** exhibit -- bursty heap allocation from Apache POI / PDF generation making garbage collection visible -- lands with **PR-2**'s report workload, which enriches the Heap and GC panels here. All panels read the Prometheus datasource; `reports` is an opt-in compose profile, so panels show *No data* when it is not up (expected, RFC-0001 D10).

panels.title: Service Up
panels.description: up{job="reports"} -- Prometheus scrape health (observability/prometheus.yml `reports` job). 0/down when the `reports` compose profile is not running (RFC-0001 D10 graceful degradation), 1 while it is scraped successfully.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: process_uptime_seconds -- time since the JVM started. The JVM's startup time (relative to the Go/Rust services) is itself part of the D2 lesson.

panels.title: Live Threads
panels.description: jvm_threads_live_threads -- current live thread count (daemon + non-daemon). Virtual threads are enabled (spring.threads.virtual), so platform-thread growth under load stays modest -- a thing to watch once PR-2 adds the blocking report workload.

panels.title: Heap Used
panels.description: sum(jvm_memory_used_bytes{area="heap"}) -- current heap occupancy across all pools. The sawtooth between GC cycles becomes pronounced with PR-2's bursty allocation.

panels.title: JVM Heap: Used vs Committed
panels.description: sum by state of jvm_memory_used_bytes / jvm_memory_committed_bytes for area="heap". Used tracks live objects; committed is what the OS has handed the heap. The gap and the used-line sawtooth are the GC-visibility exhibit (RFC-0001 D2), most pronounced once PR-2's report generation allocates in bursts.

panels.title: JVM Non-Heap Used
panels.description: sum(jvm_memory_used_bytes{area="nonheap"}) -- metaspace, code cache, etc. Grows during class loading at startup, then flattens -- a contrast to the heap's sawtooth.

panels.title: GC Pause Rate by Action
panels.description: sum(rate(jvm_gc_pause_seconds_count[5m])) by (action) -- how often GC pauses happen, split by action (end of minor/major GC). Near-flat on the idle skeleton; PR-2's allocation bursts drive it up -- the counterpart to the heap sawtooth.

panels.title: GC Time Spent by Action
panels.description: sum(rate(jvm_gc_pause_seconds_sum[5m])) by (action) -- seconds spent in GC per second of wall clock (pause-time fraction). A rising line is time the application is paused for GC; the metric to watch when tuning heap size against the container limit (RFC-0001 D2).

panels.title: HTTP Request Rate by Status
panels.description: sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count[5m])) by (status) -- Micrometer's server-side request rate. On the skeleton this is mostly the /healthz, /readyz, /metrics probe traffic; PR-2 adds the /reports API.

panels.title: HTTP Request Latency p95
panels.description: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) -- 95th-percentile server request latency. Buckets are published via management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram (application.yml).
